mechanism: Sacubitril (ARNI) causes vasodilation and hypotension, while oxybutynin (anticholinergic) reduces parasympathetic activity; combined use increases orthostatic hypotension and syncope risk.
action: Monitor blood pressure closely, counsel patient on fall prevention and orthostatic precautions, consider alternative anticholinergic with less systemic absorption (e.g., topical), and ensure adequate hydration.
